event.title: Lionel Messi Announces Retirement from International Soccer After 21 Years
event.canonical_title: Lionel Messi Announces Retirement from International Soccer After 21 Years
event.summary: Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international soccer, concluding a remarkable 21-year career with the Argentina national team. The decision follows his participation in six World Cups and scoring 98 international goals, including leading Argentina to the World Cup final in July. Messi shared the news via social media, expressing the emotional weight of his choice.

timeline.summary: Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football at the age of 39, concluding a remarkable 21-year career with Argentina. He leaves as the nation's record appearance holder and top scorer, having recently led the team to the 2026 World Cup final. Messi expressed that the decision was difficult but felt it was the right time to step away from the national team.

event_overview.title: About International Soccer
event_overview.subject: International Soccer
event_overview.summary: This event concerns Lionel Messi’s reported decision to end his international career with Argentina’s senior men’s national team, following a tenure that began with his debut in August 2005. It marks a national-team career rather than a retirement from all professional club football, and follows a period in which Messi was central to Argentina’s major tournament successes.

facts.label: International-career dates
facts.value: Messi made his senior Argentina debut against Hungary in Budapest on 17 August 2005; the selected timeline places the reported end of that international career on 31 August 2026.

facts.label: National-team context
facts.value: Argentina’s national side is administered by the Argentine Football Association (AFA), one of FIFA’s member associations; FIFA’s member associations organize and govern football within their territories.

facts.label: Major senior honours
facts.value: During Messi’s Argentina career, the team won the 2021 Copa América in Brazil and the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar; FIFA describes him as Argentina’s captain during this successful period.

facts.label: International-football governance
facts.value: FIFA is the global governing body whose statutes and regulations govern international association football, while national associations participate through six continental confederations, including South America’s CONMEBOL.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the reported retirement announcement and immediate related developments, not Messi’s full club career, every Argentina match, or the broader history of international football.
